data.title: 'Nobody Knows,' Says Investor on Anthropic Stock
data.description:
Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) got the welcome every company dreams of on its first day on the public markets. A day later, it is getting treated like every other AI stock this fall. The Claude maker priced its offering above the expected range on Wednesday, and buyers rushed in when it began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday. By Friday morning, a wide tech selloff and renewed doubts about the AI trade were pulling shares lower.

The stock opened at $111.50 on Thursday, 34% above its $83 IPO price. It ended the session at $97.17, still a 17% gain. At the time of writing, it is down by 12% in Friday's trading. That's quite a welcome to the current volatile AI market.

Against this backdrop, investor Kenio Fontes has been taking a look at this hyped stock and doesn't doubt that the business is the real thing.

Third-quarter revenue reached $17.0 billion, up 1,127% year over year. Net revenue retention is about 900%, which means existing customers are spending roughly nine times what they spent a year ago. More than 11,900 customers now pay $100,000 or more a year, compared with about 950 a year earlier. Fontes sees this as proof that a premium model provider can stand out in a market full of free and cheap options. He also thinks Claude could grow into a full enterprise platform, which would make customers harder to lose.

The trouble starts when he tries to put a value on all that. His generous long-term case has Anthropic reaching 30,000 large customers worldwide by 2036, with spending per customer compounding about 10% a year and an adjusted operating margin of 35% once the business matures. That gets him to about $176 billion in adjusted operating income. It's a solid figure, but it already assumes strong execution, and investors would have to wait a decade for it.

He also works from the top down. Anthropic's prospectus values global knowledge work at more than $40 trillion. After his own assumptions about adoption, productivity gains and the share AI providers can charge, Fontes ends up with about $100 billion in potential revenue for Anthropic. New Street Research, by contrast, expects revenue above $500 billion by 2030. To Fontes, that gap is the whole problem. The valuation can look fair if you believe the bigger numbers, but nobody knows how large the market will be or how much of it Anthropic will keep.

Competition worries him most. With OpenAI, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta all in the race, he doubts Anthropic can hold even a 20% to 30% share for the long run. Stock-based compensation is another concern. The adjusted figures leave it out, and under GAAP accounting Anthropic posted a $1.26 billion operating loss over the first nine months of 2026.

Fontes notes that the IPO cash gives Anthropic a clean balance sheet and makes near-term borrowing or dilution less likely. But he sees no margin of safety at this price. He would rather keep his exposure to Anthropic through his holdings in Amazon, Alphabet and Nvidia.

That leaves Fontes with a Sell rating on Anthropic stock. (To watch Fontes's track record, click here)

However, none of the Street's analysts are on the same page here. So far, based on 6 Buys vs. 1 Hold, the stock claims a Strong Buy consensus rating. Going by the $133.33 average price target, a year from now, shares will be changing hands for a 57% premium. (See ANT stock forecast)

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed in this article are solely those of the featured investor. The content is intended to be used for informational purposes only. It is very important to do your own analysis before making any investment.

data.title: Nvidia (NVDA) Drops Below Google to Become Fourth Most Valuable Company as Stock Plummets
data.description:
The relentless selling of Nvidia's (NVDA) stock has pushed the company's valuation lower, dropping it below Google parent company Alphabet (GOOGL) to become the fourth most valuable publicly traded company. As recently as September of this year, Nvidia was the world's most valuable company with a market capitalization above $5 trillion.

But now, Nvidia's market cap sits at $3.27 trillion, placing it behind Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet on the market cap list, according to data from Reuters (TRI). The decline in valuation comes after NVDA stock fell 15% over the past week, including a 7% drop on Nov. 20. Nvidia's stock is now at its lowest level since June 2025.

How Low Can It Go?

extending a recent selloff that dragged the chip giant down to fourth on the list of the most valuable U.S. public companies at one point on Friday, surrendering the position to Google-parent Alphabet.

As recently as last month, Nvidia held the top spot, but has since fallen behind iPhone maker Apple and software titan Microsoft.

The California-based group, whose cutting-edge semiconductors have turned it into one of the lynchpins of the global AI boom, has slumped since former CEO Jensen Huang was ousted earlier this month. The rockstar tech executive exited the firm after revelations surfaced that he had extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy and another reportedly with an employee.

Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter are both due to appear before U.S. Congressional committees early next month, where they could face sharp questions over the company's business operations with China. The U.S. government has also moved to tighten restrictions on the remote access Chinese firms have to high-end processors, such as those made by Nvidia.

Coupled with the leadership scandal, investors have also been making bets that Democrats may use their sweeping victories in the U.S. midterm elections to slow down data center development.

Against this backdrop, shares of Nvidia have shed more than a fourth of their value this month alone, erasing more than a trillion dollars' worth of market capitalization in the process. The decline has contributed to overall dour sentiment around the AI trade that contributed to potentially the worst run in global stocks since 2023. Tech names sold off again on Friday, with the Nasdaq Composite last down by 1.5%.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Nvidia, AMD, and Broadcom Lead AI Chip Selloff as Shares Plunge Up to 10%
data.description:
Chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and Broadcom (AVGO) led a sharp selloff in semiconductor stocks on Friday, with Nvidia heading for its seventh consecutive losing session. AMD and Broadcom shares each plunged by roughly 10% as selling pressure spread throughout the AI industry. The declines followed Thursday's stock market debut of AI developer Anthropic (ANT), which added to existing worries about AI spending and the future profitability of the technology.

The selling comes as questions grow about how technology companies will finance their enormous AI investments. Nvidia is also dealing with a leadership change after founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO last week. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO while the company searches for a permanent replacement.

However, Nvidia's latest results suggest that customer demand remains strong. Third-quarter revenue grew by 103% from a year earlier to $115.8 billion, while data center sales increased by 110% to $107.6 billion. The company also forecast $130 billion in revenue for the current quarter.

Why the AI Selloff Is Spreading to Other Chip Stocks

Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives described the decline as a "panic-driven sell-off" rather than a sign that the AI spending cycle is ending. He estimates that Big Tech capital expenditures could reach $1.5 trillion in 2027, despite the recent stock market weakness.

For now, the selling has reached most of the semiconductor industry. Memory-chip producer Micron Technology (MU) dropped by more than 3%, while contract chip manufacturer Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) and Dutch equipment supplier ASML (ASML) also declined. U.S. chipmaker Intel (INTC) traded lower as well.

AMD faced additional pressure after Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a short position and questioned whether the company's chips were reaching restricted Chinese customers through intermediaries. AMD has said that it follows applicable U.S. export-control laws.

The weakness has also spread to companies that rent computing power to AI developers. Data center operators CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) both fell by roughly 9%, as concerns about financing expensive infrastructure projects continued to weigh on the sector.

Meanwhile, optical equipment supplier Coherent (COHR) slid by about 6%, while fuel-cell maker Bloom Energy (BE) declined by roughly 7%. Nvidia is now down approximately 22% since the start of 2026. This puts it on pace for its first annual decline since 2022.

What Is a Good Price for NVDA?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on Nvidia stock based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell assigned in the past three months. Furthermore, the average Nvidia price target of $232.59 per share implies 71% upside potential. (See NVDA Stock Forecast).

data.title: Amazon Stock (AMZN) Slips Despite the E-Commerce Giant Launching Black Friday and Cyber Monday Deals Early
data.description:
Amazon (AMZN) stock was down slightly on Friday after the company launched its Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals. While Black Friday is still a week away, Amazon is getting an early start. This is part of the company's ongoing plan to extend the holiday shopping season, which saw it start introducing special deals earlier this month.

Amazon's Black Friday and Cyber Monday discount event started on Thursday and will last through Nov. 30, 2026. The company noted that the special event covers large brands across various sectors. It also highlighted special offers only available on Amazon, including Swarovski jewelry, Caraway cookware sets, necklaces from Spicy Dan, and the NAADAM Originals cashmere crewneck in medium blue.

In addition to these deals, Amazon will roll out more discounts and special offers over the next several days. That includes deals that refresh frequently throughout the deal. The company also said that this will be the first year that it introduces discounts of up to 60% on goods at midnight ET on Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

Heading into the holiday shopping seasons, Amazon is facing trouble in one of its largest areas. New York City has introduced a new bill that would require the company to hire delivery drivers who work for it on a contract basis. The company said this could add as much as $5 per order to costs. It also threatened to leave NYC over the proposed bill.

Amazon Black Friday and Cyber Monday Deals

Amazon is offering steep discounts on select goods to appeal to customers during the holiday shopping season. A few examples include:

  • Up to $600 off on select TVs from Sony (SONY) and Hisense (HISEF).
  • Up to 50% off on select headphones and speakers from Beats, JBL, Marshall, and Sonos (SONO).
  • Up to 30% off on select laptops and gaming PCs from ASUS (ASUUY), ACER, Alienware, Lenovo (LNVGY), and HP (HPQ).
  • Up to 45% off on select toys from NERF, Play-Doh, MAGNA-TILES, and Mattel (MAT).
  • Up to 40% off on select cookware from Our Place and Farberware.

Is Amazon Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold Today?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for Amazon is Strong Buy, based on 42 Buy ratings and one Hold rating over the past three months. With that comes an average AMZN stock price target of $325.02, suggesting a possible 27.76% upside for the shares. (See AMZN Stock Forecast)

data.title: Nike (NKE) Named Official Partner of Formula 1 Race Car Circuit
data.description:
Nike (NKE) has been named the new official partner of the Formula 1 (FWONK) race car circuit. In a statement, Nike said that the partnership will give it a new promotional outlet and Formula 1 new ways to monetize its global brand. Starting with the 2027 race season, Nike will outfit racing staff, launch new Formula 1-inspired collections, and create race-weekend experiences to engage fans of the racing sport.

"Formula 1 is driven by competition, speed, and a constant push to innovate," says Nike CEO Elliott Hill in the company's statement. ""That's an athlete mindset, and it's one we share at Nike. Together, we have an incredible opportunity to bring new energy to the sport, serve its athletes, and inspire fans around the world."

Above is a chart from TipRanks that looks at the performance of Nike's stock in 2026. As one can see, the company's share price has fallen 44% year-to-date.

Formula 1 Has Global Reach

Formula1 racing is one of the most popular sports around the world and second only to soccer in its reach. Formula 1 drew a global audience of 1.83 billion viewers during the 2025 season, averaging 76.1 million viewers per Grand Prix race, according to the Nielsen ratings company.

Nike's new partnership with Formula 1 will officially begin on Nov. 20 of this year at the Las Vegas Grand Prix event. The collection will be available at the Nike Las Vegas store at Caesars Palace resort and Casino, and the F1 Hub at The Venetian Resort, said Nike.

A Boost for Nike

Nike added that it will also be the official sportswear partner of F1 ACADEMY, the all-female racing series. For Nike, the new partnership with Formula 1 comes at an important time for the sneaker maker. CEO Hill recently appealed to shareholders and investors to be patient as the company undertakes a multi-year turnaround strategy.

Anthony Berni, an analyst at Jefferies Financial Group (JEF) was supportive of Nike's Formula 1 partnership. In a note to clients, Berni wrote, "Nike's sponsorship deal reinforces our view that sponsorship remains an attractive source of asset-light growth." Jefferies has a Buy rating and $60 price target on NKE stock, which is 77% higher than where the shares currently trade.

Is NKE Stock a Buy?

Nike's stock has a consensus Hold rating among 37 Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on nine Buy, 18 Hold, and 10 Sell recommendations issued in the last three months. The average NKE price target of $36.73 implies less than 1% upside from current levels.

data.title: AMD Stock Drops After Hunterbrook Report — Who Still Owns the Chipmaker?
data.description:
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock fell at Friday's market open, extending losses from the previous session. The decline came after short seller Hunterbrook Media said AMD has a "China problem" and disclosed that it had taken a short position in the stock. The report also warned that new U.S. export rules could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business."

The report claims that more than 20% of AMD's revenue comes from customers in China and Hong Kong. It also says the company relies on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.

 This article looks at who owns AMD stock using TipRanks' Ownership Tool.

Who Owns AMD Stock?

According to TipRanks' Ownership Tool, public companies and individual investors own 30.97% of AMD. They are followed by ETFs at 29.25% and other institutional investors at 20.74%. Mutual funds hold 18.63%, while insiders hold the remaining 0.41%.

Public companies and individual investors make up the largest ownership group, followed by ETFs and other institutional investors.

Breaking Down AMD's Ownership Structure

Looking closely at top shareholders, BlackRock (BLK) owns the highest stake in AMD at 9.30%. Next up is Vanguard, which holds a 7.95% stake in the company.

Within ETF holders, the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) owns 2.65%, while theVanguard Total Stock Market ETF (VTI) owns a 2.49%. Among mutual funds, Vanguard Index Funds holds about 6.89% of AMD. Meanwhile, Fidelity Concord Street Trust owns 1.79% of the company.

AMD Stock Performance

AMD stock has gained over 120% so far in 2026, reaching $451 as of November 20. However, the stock is down 30% from its 52-week high of $658.52, reached in October. Recent swings in AI and chip stocks weigh on shares.

AMD has a market value of $802.31 billion. Its 52-week trading range is $188.22 to $658.52, and its average daily trading volume over the past three months is 32.82 million shares.

Is AMD Stock a Buy or Sell Now?   

According to TipRanks, AMD stock has a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on 29 Buys and three Holds. The average AMD stock price target of $652.18 indicates a possible upside of 46.6% from current levels.

data.title: PayPal Stock (PYPL) Dips 2% on CFO and Other Executive Changes
data.description:
PayPal (PYPL) stock decreased 1.9% on Friday after the payment services company announced that Claire Bramley will take over as the next Chief Financial Officer of the company. This will have Bramley replace CFO and Chief Operating Officer Jamie Miller. Bramley will join the company on Feb. 1, 2027, and will work closely with Miller through February to ensure a smooth transition.

Bramley will join PayPal from Xero (XROLF), which is a global small-business platform, where she was CFO since April 2025. Before that, Bramley was the CFO of Teradata (TDC) and also held senior finance roles at HP (HPQ).

Outside of Bramley as its new CFO, PayPal also announced several other leadership changes.

  • Kartik Mani will join the company from American Express (AXP) as its new President and Head of Consumer Financial Services & Venmo.
  • Suzan Kereere will leave the Global Markets role at PayPal to take over as its new President and Head of Payment Services & Crypto.
  • Juan Rio will join PayPal from Brightstar.AI as its new EVP of AI Business Transformation & Operations.
  • Aaron Webster, PayPal's Chief Risk Officer will depart the company, with Ratinder Bedi, SVP of Credit and Fraud Risk, acting as interim head until a replacement is found.

What's Behind the PayPal Leadership Changes?

PayPal said there are a few reasons that it has switched up its executives. The company wants to establish clear strategies across its core businesses, simplify its operating model, and align leadership accountability with its long-term priorities.

"We've made significant progress in defining where we want to take PayPal and how we will compete and win," said Enrique Lores, President and CEO of PayPal. "With our three-year strategies in place, our focus is now on execution. These appointments bring together experienced leaders with the capabilities to accelerate innovation, strengthen our businesses and deliver greater value to our customers and shareholders."

Is PayPal Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold on Today's News?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for PayPal is Hold, based on three Buy, 19 Hold, and five Sell ratings over the past three months. With that comes an average PYPL stock price target of $57.65, suggesting a possible 4.88% upside for the shares. (See PYPL Stock Forecast)

data.title: IREN Stock Plunges 62% YTD — Why Bernstein Says to Buy
data.description:
Shares of Australian data center operator IREN Limited (IREN) have fallen by roughly 62% since the start of the year. IREN recently shifted its annual recurring revenue (ARR) target from year-end to January 2027. This added to pressure on the stock. However, Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei maintained her Buy rating on IREN shares on Thursday. She also kept her price target at $55, suggesting about 306% upside. She argued that while short-term ARR timing has shifted, actual computing capacity remains contracted and funded.

Why IREN Shares Have Sold Off This Year

Since the start of the year, IREN shares have faced several pressure points that have dragged down their value. The company recently revealed a funding gap. It plans to spend $15 billion in fiscal 2027. It expects about $9 billion to come from cash and secured financing. That leaves a $6 billion funding gap.

Most recently, data center stocks sold off after Democrats regained control of Congress. This sparked fears of political pushback against data center expansion.

Another reason is investor concern about high borrowing costs. Last month, IREN stock plunged after data showed that yields on rival CoreWeave's (CRWV) bonds due in 2032 had reached a record high.

What's more, a recent warning from Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX (SPCX) and Tesla (TSLA), also added to the pressure. Musk said more than 200 neocloud companies could face "guppy-level death" or be forced to combine forces. This is because lenders are pulling back from AI cloud firms without significant revenue sources outside AI data centers.

Reports that Microsoft (MSFT) was tightening oversight of data center projects by neocloud companies did not help matters, either.

Bernstein Is Bullish on IREN's 'Capital Discipline'

At its fiscal Q1 2027 earnings call, IREN said it plans to spend $15 billion on capital expenses for the rest of the fiscal year. This marked a reduction from its prior forecast.

Rezaei sees the slower spending pace as "capital discipline rather than a sign of weaker demand."

Is IREN a Good Stock to Buy Now?

On Wall Street, analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on IREN's shares. This reflects eight Buys and three Holds assigned over the past three months.

However, the average IREN price target of $67.00 implies about 272% upside ahead (see IREN stock forecast here).

data.title: Zoom (ZM) vs. Twilio (TWLO): Which Communications Stock Offers More Upside?
data.description:
Zoom Communications (ZM) is reporting earnings next week, and investors will be watching for updates on the company's growth outlook and its push beyond video conferencing. Twilio (TWLO) offers a different way to invest in communications, providing software that helps businesses engage customers through messaging, voice, and email. We compare the two stocks using the TipRanks Stock Comparison tool to see which offers more upside, according to analysts.

The comparison also shows that the two companies have market capitalizations in a similar range, making the comparison more relevant.

Is ZM a Buy Ahead of Earnings?

Zoom Communications runs the video calling and chat platform that millions of people and companies rely on for remote work, online classes, and virtual meetings. Beyond basic video calls, it sells businesses a full suite of workplace tools, including cloud phone systems, team messaging, and artificial intelligence (AI) meeting assistants. The company is set to report Q3 FY2027 earnings on November 23. According to the TipRanks forecast data, analysts estimate sales of $1.28 billion and earnings per share (EPS) of $1.49.

In its investor session last month, Zoom said it targets 6%–8% annual revenue growth by Fiscal 2030, with double-digit Enterprise growth, a non-GAAP operating margin of around 40%, and a GAAP operating margin of 28%–30%. On TipRanks, ZM has a Moderate Buy consensus, with 13 analysts rating the stock a Buy and nine rating it a Hold. The average ZM stock price target of $119.17 implies an upside of 44.62%.

Is TWLO a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Twilio provides the behind-the-scenes software tools that companies use to build text messaging, voice calls, and email directly into their own apps. When you get a two-factor login code via text, receive an appointment reminder, or message your rideshare driver without seeing their real phone number, Twilio's technology is usually powering it in the background. In its Q3 2026 earnings released last month, it reported revenue of $1,560 million and EPS of $1.65. For full-year 2026, it raised revenue growth from 18%–18.5% previously to 20% year-over-year.

Twilio's top customer wins in Q3 included a health insurer that signed its first eight-figure Conversations deal to run a voice AI agent, along with AI-native firms such as ElevenLabs, Gong, and Ushur that expanded their usage. Looking ahead, TWLO has a Moderate Buy consensus from 19 Wall Street analysts, with 15 rating it a Buy, three rating it a Hold, and one rating it a Sell. The average price target of $269.39 suggests a 50.34% upside from the last price.

Conclusion

The next few quarters are important for both companies. Zoom needs to show that its expansion beyond video conferencing is gaining traction, while Twilio will be looking to build on demand for its customer-communications software. The data above offers a side-by-side view of where each company stands today. Wall Street is bullish on both stocks, but currently sees more upside in TWLO.
